  exactly as before.
- **Checks made as you type, switch tabs or follow a link look at the disk in the background.** A Markdown file's
  lint settings, `.editorconfig` rules, Markdown and HTTP completion, spelling verdicts, a language server's project
  folder and its Java project checks, links followed in Markdown, the terminal, the console and the agent's
  transcript, Go to Super Method, the New Maven Project form, the SSH Connect form's Host field, Find in Files' folder,
  the Problems window, the Map's tooltips, Local File History's view of a closed file, a log followed from its end,
  the JDK lists, keymap switches, zoomed stylesheets, Reload User Themes, Settings sync and the debugger's frame
  checks no longer wait for the disk on the UI thread. What you may notice: the first lint of a file in a folder not
  seen before, a new misspelling's squiggle and a Markdown completion list appear a moment later; the SSH form fills
  the user and port once you pause typing; a Map tooltip shows the size and date when they arrive; on the first
  right-click of a folder outside any Maven project the Maven submenu can show briefly before it hides; a popup first
  opened at a zoom other than 100% can show at 100% for a moment; a bundled font picked before the rest are loaded
  shows in the fallback face until it is. A Run, Build or Debug command in a folder not looked at yet, a keymap
  switch in the first moments after launch, Markdown lint's Fix and a `.http` run start once the background look or
  parse lands; New Maven Project's Create waits until the folder has been checked, and a terminal link click on a path
  waits for the path to be checked. A Settings row for a server command or debugger path you just typed says
  "checking" until it is found. A save follows the `.editorconfig` as it is on disk at that moment.
- **File commands, installs and plugins work on disk in the background.** Opening, renaming, moving and deleting
  files in the Project panel and on the Map, New Folder, New ▸ type, Save As's "replace it?" check, Revert, Rename
  File, Reopen Closed Tab, Go to Related File and Create Test, Find File's Enter on a typed path, a bookmark or a
  personal note on a file that is not open, Local History's copy before a delete, its folder view and Recent
  Changes, a pasted or dropped image in Markdown, a merge resolution applied after its file's tab was closed, the
  Diff commands, Git Clone and Init's folder checks, Export to HTML, CSV and JSON, Save Output, the HTML preview's
  site folder, a Typst export put in place, the Run Configurations Browse button, the follow-up of New Maven Project
  and Maven Update Versions on a closed pom, a language server's refactoring and Undo Last Refactoring, plugin
  installs, updates, removals and the plugin list's Reload, the install commands' "is it installed already?"
  checks, Settings → Language Servers' status lines and the Doctor's look at its rows all read, write and look at
  files in the background, then show the result. While one of them is under way, pressing it again starts nothing
  a second time. A rename or a move in the Project panel moves the file first and its tabs follow once it is
  there, as before. A dialog's start folder is no longer checked before the dialog opens; a folder that is gone is
  dropped and the dialog opens where the system puts it. The spelling suggestions of a right-click always arrive
  in the menu's "Searching…" row.
- **Run, Build, Debug and the other programs Editora starts are started in the background.** Finding the program on
  your PATH, starting it and recording it for clean-up no longer happen on the UI thread, for Run, Build, the
  program a debugger hands back, Run in Terminal, a program in a container or a WSL distribution, and the New Maven
  Project generation. Run's and Build's Stop applies from the moment you press Run: a press while the program is
  still starting does not start a second one, and a Stop then ends it as soon as it has started. Run's input field
  opens once the program has started. A build looks for its wrapper and reads what the trust question lists in the
  background, then asks. Maven Update Versions reads the pom in the background before it says "Checking…", the Git
  Log checks for a shallow clone in the background, a Java debug launch reads the file's main class and the class
  files it warns about in the background, and a Kotlin program is hashed and its jar looked up in the background.
  A program in a Terminal tab that cannot start ends its tab with the error, as one on another machine does.
  Closing a shell tab asks what the shell runs in the background, then asks you. Deleting files in the Project
  panel (to the trash, `gio trash` included) happens in the background, then reports. The login shell's PATH is
  read as Editora starts, and a command given before it is known uses the PATH Editora was started with. The MCP
  endpoint file is written and removed in the background, and the MCP server starts in the background (the status
  bar shows it once it runs). A Git command given before Git was first checked no longer waits for `git --version`.
  What Run and Debug read before a launch — the configuration's script and folder, an environment `@file`, the
  shebang, the build files and the Maven reactor, `launch.json`, `tasks.json`, `debug-adapters.json`, a Go, Rust,
  C/C++ or C# project — is read in the background too, and so are Export and Import Breakpoints, Add to
  .gitignore, the conflict-marker check before staging, the "replace it?" checks of the encryption commands and
  New Maven Project's folder, pom and archetype reads and its move into place. Quitting or closing a window with
  busy terminals asks from what each terminal last reported; a terminal on another machine that never answered
  yet is not listed.
- **Settings and the other stores are saved in the background.** Changing a setting, showing a tool window,
  setting a bookmark or a breakpoint, writing a note, saving a macro, trusting a folder, adding a word to the
  dictionary and focusing or opening a window no longer wait for the config folder: the change applies at once and
  is written by the config writer, in order, and the last of it when Editora quits. Closing one window no longer
  waits for its session to be written. A window opened by a command (New Window, Open Project, a launch from the
  file manager) is built once its session has been read in the background; asking again while it is read opens
  one window, not two. Saving `settings.json` in a tab, a project's own settings, the snippet and template files,
  the Project Map's trails and Export and Import of shared run configurations read and write in the background too;
  the Trails menu shows "Loading…" until the trails are listed, and a language's snippets are read when a file of it
  opens. Words another Editora added to the dictionary now join this one's when it writes the file.
- **More of start-up's disk work is done off the UI thread.** Opening the session log, the claim on the config
  folder, cleaning up after a crashed run, reading your own themes, the recent files and the search history, making
  the zoomed stylesheets and checking the installed language servers, debuggers and configured tools now happen on
  the thread that loads the settings while the toolkit starts, before the first window is built. Windows restored
  after the first read their sessions in the background, later windows reuse the app icons, and the Welcome page
  checks which recent files and projects still exist in the background.
- **Three long lists build only the rows on screen.** The shortcut list in Settings ▸ Keymaps, the list of a
  pull request's checks and the crontab preview made a row for every command, check or job, and the shortcut list
  made them all again at each key typed in its filter. Each is now a list that builds the rows it shows.
  - Shortcuts: the list is still one Tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End walk it, Enter or Space selects a row
    and a second Enter records, Delete unbinds. A command title too long for its row ends in an ellipsis where it
    used to wrap.
  - Checks: the list is one Tab stop. The arrow keys move along the checks and Enter opens the selected check's
    failure log, or its page on GitHub when it did not fail; the links of the rows on screen are still Tab stops.
  - Crontab: the preview reads as before; a row's text wraps to the preview's width.
- **A window builds less before it shows.** The cards of the command palette and the other pickers, the Settings
  window, the Message Log, the Doctor page and the shared Output console are now built the first time each is
  opened (the Output console also by the first build or Git command that writes to it), and the Welcome page only
  in a window that opens on no file.
- **Editora asks before more removals that used to happen at once.** Each of these now asks first, names what
  goes, and keeps it when you press Cancel or Enter: deleting a Git branch that is fully merged (a branch with
  unmerged commits is still asked about once, with the count); Remove All for the trusted folders; Reset draft
  in a diff's result editor, when the draft has edits; Remove All Watches and Unmark All Objects in the debugger;
  deleting a run configuration, and removing one, a deployment, a compound or a type renderer from its list;
  removing a stop from a Project Map trail and deleting a working set; Restore Default Layout for the tool
  windows and for the toolbar, unless the layout already is the default one; Remove from URL and Disconnect on the
  Sync page; New Token for the MCP server; Revert on the Macros page, when the macro has unsaved changes; Remove
  Manual Fold Ranges, when the file has any; and Clear in the HTTP panel, when it keeps responses. Importing run configurations from the project asks only when
  it would replace a configuration or a deployment of this window with a different one, and says how many.
  Exporting them asks only when the project's shared file is there and says something else, and saving a Project
  Map working set under a name already taken asks only when that set shows something else.
- **A menu bar row that cannot run says why.** A command with nothing to act on, or whose feature is switched
  off, stays grayed in its menu as before, but hovering it now shows the reason, the same sentence the Command
  Palette gives ("the active file is not inside a Git repository"), a screen reader hears it with the row, and
  choosing it says it in the status bar instead of doing nothing. On macOS, where the menus are the system's,
  such a row is still only disabled.
- **A grayed row of a right-click menu or a drop-down says why, too.** Cut with nothing selected, Close Tabs to
  the Left on the first tab, the Git submenu of a file outside any repository, Revert on a clean file, a Map card's
  Hierarchy on a file whose language has no callers: each still looks as it did, but hovering it shows why
  ("Nothing is selected.", "There are no changes to revert here."), a screen reader hears the reason with the row,
  the arrow keys stop on it, and choosing it says it in the status bar and closes the menu instead of doing
  nothing. The command behind such a row, run from the Command Palette or a key, says the same sentence. A text
  field's own right-click menu explains its grayed Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Delete the same way. Rows that
  only say something ("No recent files") are unchanged.
- **Every menu's rows line up like the menu bar's.** Right-click menus and drop-downs drew their rows the
  theme's way, with the glyph 6 px from the title, no column when a row had no glyph, and the keys 14 px after the
  title. Their rows now have the menu bar's layout: a 22 px column for the glyph, kept on a row without one, 8 px
  to the title, and the keys 18 px or more after the titles. A check or radio row's tick sits in that same column,
  also in a menu that has both ticks and glyphs. The sizes follow the interface zoom.
- **The Command Palette and the pickers tell a screen reader which row is selected.** The arrow keys move
  a highlight while the keyboard stays in the text field, so a screen reader said nothing. The list now
  announces the row, each palette row has a spoken name (its title and its keys), and a command that cannot
  run says so with the reason.
- **Editora follows the system's reduced-motion setting.** With it on, the ring that fades around a row
  revealed in the Project Map is not shown; turning the setting on while it fades removes it at once.
- **Your templates and snippet files say which format they are in.** A template you save and a snippet
  file Editora writes now carry `"schemaVersion": 1`; files from before load as they always did, and the
  marker is added the next time Editora saves them. If a newer Editora ever changes the format, an older one
  no longer misreads its files: a template or snippet file from a newer version is not loaded, is left
  exactly as it is, and a copy is kept beside it (`<name>.v<n>.bak`). Saving into such a snippet file is
  refused, and Settings Sync does not merge one.
- **Find in a console or a Project Map card highlights every match.** Only the current match was selected;
  now all of them are highlighted while the find bar is open, the current one more strongly, as in the
  editor. Output that arrives while the bar is open is highlighted and counted too.
- **A problem report says how Editora is set up.** Help → Report a Problem and `editora --report` now end
  the system details with one line of settings: the theme, the language, the keymap, the interface zoom, and
  which features are on (language servers, debugging, Git, plugins, AI and so on). It holds no path, address
  or key. `--report` reads it from the settings file, and says so when that file cannot be read.
- **Welcome Page is in the Help menu.** It moved from the View menu, in the full menu bar and in Simple
  mode, and the Help menu's rows now run in one order: Command Palette, Documentation, Keyboard Shortcuts,
  Welcome Page, Check for Updates, Message Log, Debug Log, Report a Problem, Pauta Conformance, About.
- **Three choices are asked in the picker instead of a system dialog.** The mode of a Git reset (soft,
  mixed, hard, each with what it keeps), the parent to keep when reverting a merge commit, and the settings
  backup to restore now open the same picker every other list choice uses: type to filter, Enter to choose,
  Esc to cancel. The reset opens on mixed, as before.
- **Dates and numbers keep your system's region.** Editora wrote them the way the bare interface language
  does: an Austrian system got German formats, and choosing English on a French system changed every date.
  They now follow the system: its region is kept when no language is chosen in Settings or the chosen one
  is the system's own, and only another language brings its own formats. Numbers inside messages follow
  the same rule as the rest of the window.
- **Modifier keys are named the same in every language.** The German, Spanish, French and Italian
  translations said Strg, Umschalt, Mayús, Maj and Maiusc where the key caps, the keymaps and the docs say
  Ctrl and Shift, and translated Option on a Mac. They now read Ctrl, Shift, Control and Option everywhere.
- **A mistyped option on the command line stops the launch.** `editora --config-dri /tmp/x` used to ignore
  the option it did not know and start on your real settings. It now prints `Editora: unknown option:
  --config-dri` and how to get help, and exits with status 2 before any window opens. This holds for an option
  with one dash too. The JVM options a launcher can leave among the arguments (`--add-exports`,
  `--add-opens`, `-p`) are still passed over, with their values.
- **`--new-file` and `--diff-ui` use the Editora already running.** `editora --new-file` and `editora
  --diff-ui LEFT RIGHT` each started a second Editora on the same settings. They now open their window (the
  new buffer, the comparison) in the one already running, as a launch with files does. `--new-instance` still
  starts a separate one, and so does `--disable-plugins`.
- **Every tooltip appears after the same short wait.** Tooltips on labels, list rows, badges, tabs and the
  status bar waited a full second, while buttons and gutter markers answered in 400 ms. All of them now show
  after 400 ms.
- **Toolbar buttons are greyed out when they cannot do anything.** Save As and the split buttons with no
  file in front, and a button you added to the toolbar whose command has nothing to act on (Commit or Git Log
  outside a repository, a tool window whose feature is off), are now disabled, as their menu rows are. Save
  and Save As are greyed out in the menus and the command palette too while no file is in front.
- **A tool window's stripe button and its command do the same thing.** A click on a stripe button now runs
  the window's command instead of toggling the panel past it. So a button does not open a panel whose
  feature is off (Debug, the language-server windows, Personal Notes, Commit, GitHub, the AI Agent) or the
  TODO window for a file with no matches: it says why in the status bar, as the command does. Remote Sites
  is refreshed when its button opens it. A window that is on screen always hides on its button. The
  Terminal's button is unchanged.
- **Tool Window: Git Log and the build tools' commands hide their window too.** Tool Window: Git Log, Maven,
  Gradle, Package Scripts, Cargo, Go, sbt, Mill, Scala CLI, Clojure CLI, Leiningen and Babashka only ever
  opened their window; run again they now hide it, as every other Tool Window command does. A key bound to
  one of them now toggles.
- **Zoom In, Zoom Out and Reset Zoom zoom an image or a PDF.** With an image or a PDF in the active tab, the
  three content zoom commands (and their keys) now zoom it, as its −, + and 1:1 buttons do; before, they
  changed the text zoom of editors you were not looking at.
- **Panel toolbar buttons no longer take a Tab stop.** The Project Map's Back, Forward, Help and Options, the
  Git Log's three toolbar buttons, Test Results' Follow toggle and Structure's kind filter are out of the Tab
  order now that each has a command, so Tab goes straight to the content. The Map's history list, which the
  Menu key on Back or Forward opened, is the new Project Map: History command.
- **A new run configuration starts as the type of the file in front.** Run Configurations → Add made a Java
  configuration for anything that was not a script it could propose whole. With a makefile open it now makes a
  Make target configuration, and with a `package.json` an npm script one, each set to run in that file's
  folder; a Python, shell, Node.js, Groovy, Kotlin, Scala or Clojure file not saved yet gets a configuration of
  its type as well. A file no type launches (a note, a C# file) still gets a Java one. The Type box also shows
  each type with the icon its files carry in the tabs and the Project tree.
- **A key you rebind is rebound on every system.** Your own key bindings were kept apart for macOS and for
  Windows and Linux, so a chord changed on a Mac stayed as it was on your Linux or Windows computer, even
  in the Emacs keymap, whose chords are the same everywhere. They are now one set per keymap. In a keymap
  with a macOS form (CUA, VS Code, IntelliJ, Sublime) a chord you record with Ctrl is used with Cmd on a
  Mac, and the other way round. A chord only a Mac can type (one that uses the Control key there) stays the
  Mac's own, and the other systems keep theirs. Existing bindings are converted and none is lost: where the
  two systems had different bindings for a command, each keeps its own. Settings Sync's `keybindings.json`
  changes layout with this; an older Editora will say the file was written by a newer one.
- **The VCS menu is named Git.** Git is the one version-control system Editora works with, and every row of the
  menu is a Git command. The rows and their order are unchanged.
- **Run ▸ Debugger is four submenus.** The Debugger submenu had grown to fifty rows, taller than the screen, and
  scrolled. Its rows are now grouped by what they are for:
  - **Launch and Attach:** Run and Debug Selected Configuration, Start Configuration…, Start Compound…, Edit
    Compounds…, Attach to Process…, Reattach, Debug in Browser…, Attach to Browser….
  - **Stepping:** Pause, the step commands, Run to Cursor, Force Run to Cursor, Restart Frame.
  - **Breakpoints:** Toggle Breakpoint and the other breakpoint kinds, Edit Breakpoint…, the breakpoint list, its
    groups, export and import, Mute Breakpoints, and the exception breakpoints.
  - **Debugger:** Evaluate Expression, watches and values, Debug History, and the Threads, Loaded Sources, Modules,
    Disassembly and Memory views.
  - Toggle Breakpoint, Attach to Process… and Reattach moved from the top of Run into these submenus, so Run keeps
    to twenty rows. Their keys are unchanged.
- **"Maven: New Project…" is "Maven: New Maven Project…".** In the File menu, where a row drops the command's
  "Maven:" prefix, it read "New Project…" and named no build tool; it now reads "New Maven Project…". "Maven: New
  Project in Folder…" is "Maven: New Maven Project in Folder…" to match.
- **Simple UI mode's menus no longer list Encrypt File and Toggle Comment.** The Simple File menu had "Encrypt
  File…" and the Simple Edit menu had "Toggle Comment", neither a plain editing action. Both are still in the
  full menu bar (Tools ▸ Encryption and Edit), and in Simple UI mode from the command palette and their keys.
- **One place decides which operating system Editora runs on.** Sixty-odd separate checks, spelled a
  dozen ways, now ask one class. Nothing changes on Windows, macOS or Linux; a system that is none of the
  three (a BSD) is now treated as Linux throughout, where some checks used to treat it as nothing at all.
  Starting Editora with `-Deditora.os=windows`, `mac` or `linux` runs it as that system, for testing.
- **Toolbar buttons are named after the commands they run**, with the shortcut from the active keymap, and a
  screen reader now says the same words the tooltip shows. The main toolbar's tooltips change with it: Open is
  "Find File…", Find is "Incremental Search", Close Tab is "Close", Simple UI mode is "Toggle Simple UI Mode",
  and Stop shows the shortcut of Run: Stop Program. More than 150 icon-only buttons across the panels, the
  Project Map, the diff viewer and Settings got one name for both; several had a tooltip and no name for a
  screen reader, and a few had neither.
- **Tab no longer stops on toolbar buttons.** The main toolbar, the tool window stripes, a tool window's header
  buttons and the panel toolbar buttons that a command also runs are skipped, so Tab moves through the
  content. Each is still reached by its command, the palette and the menus.
- **Button and gutter tooltips appear after the same 400 ms.** The gutter's markers used 300 ms, the diff viewer
  and the Map 350 ms, and toolbar buttons JavaFX's one second. Tooltips on labels and list rows still take a
  second.
- **A tool window stripe button's tooltip follows its window's title** (the Project window's "Current Folder").
- **Right-click menus and drop-downs show each command's keyboard shortcut beside its row**, as the menu bar
  does, read from the active keymap and from your own key bindings each time a menu opens. More than 120
  rows that showed none now show one where their command is bound: in the Commit window, the Git log, the GitHub panel, the diff
  viewer, the Debug panel, the terminal's tabs, Project Map cards and declaration rows, the editor's and a
  tab's menus, tool window headers, the HTTP Client, the CSV grid and Markdown lint. An external tool's row
  shows the shortcut you gave that tool.
- **The keymap's Copy and Select All keys work in a Project Map card.** A card answered only the built-in
  Ctrl+C and Ctrl+A (Cmd on macOS); M-w in the Emacs keymap, or a shortcut of your own, did nothing there.
- **The Menu key and Shift+F10 open the selected row's menu in every list, tree and table**, at that row, after
  scrolling it into view. In the Problems panel the keys did nothing; in the Commit window, the Debug call
  stack and threads, Test Results, the HTTP headers table, the CSV grid and several others the menu opened in
  the middle of the panel instead of at the row. Shift+F10 is the same on macOS.
- **Menu rows that delete, discard, revert or reset something are drawn in red**, in right-click menus,
  drop-downs and the menu bar: Delete in the Project panel, the Git discards and resets, Drop Stash, Delete Tag,
  Purge in Local History, deleting bookmarks and notes, removing breakpoints and watches, and the like.
- **Pressing Find again while a find bar is open goes to the next match** in the consoles and in the terminal,
  as it does in the editor. In the terminal it used to only put the cursor back in the field.
- **Typing in a console's find bar searches from where the caret was when the bar opened**, so narrowing the
  query no longer runs on down the output.
- **The keymap's editing keys work in every find field.** In the find bars of the consoles, the terminal and
  Project Map cards, C-a, C-e, C-k and C-y in the Emacs keymap (Ctrl+V/X/C/Z in the others) now act on the
  field, as they already did in the editor's.
- **Questions before something is lost are asked the same way everywhere.** The button that confirms carries the
  action's own name (Delete, Discard, Replace, Overwrite, Reset) in red, never OK, and Cancel is the default
  button: it has the focus when the question opens, so Enter keeps what you have and the red action runs only
  from its own button. Before, Enter confirmed many of them, among them the Git discards, the Local History
  purges, moving a file to the trash, Revert and overwriting a file from Save As. Where a question offers a
  safe action beside the red one (Save beside Discard, Pull then Push beside Force with Lease), the safe action
  is the default.
- **Every dialog draws its buttons in one order on Windows, macOS and Linux**, with Cancel left of every action.
  The unsaved-changes question reads Cancel, Save, Discard. JavaFX's own order differed per system.
- **Dialog buttons follow the interface language.** OK, Cancel, Yes, No, Apply and Close were worded by the Java
  runtime in the system's language, so a dialog could say "Cancel" in another language than the menus.
- **Editora asks before some removals that used to happen at once:** clearing a file's bookmarks, deleting a
  bookmark from the Bookmarks panel, taking off a bookmark that has a note, deleting a personal note at the caret
  or from the Notes panel, deleting all notes of a file, and removing a saved connection from the Remote panel.
  A plain bookmark still toggles off without a question, since the same key puts it back.
- **Deleting a remote site or an external tool says that it cannot be undone.**
- **`--dev` now wins over `EDITORA_CONFIG_DIR`.** The configuration folder is chosen in this order: `--config-dir`,
  then `--dev` (`~/.editora-dev`), then the `EDITORA_CONFIG_DIR` variable, then `~/.editora`. Before, the variable
  won over `--dev`, so a development launch from a shell that had the variable set used the everyday folder. To
  run a development instance on another folder, name it with `--config-dir`.
- **The Message Log follows the keymap for closing and copying.** It closes on Esc and on the chord your keymap
  binds to cancel (C-g in Emacs), no longer on a fixed Ctrl+G, which is Go to Line in the CUA keymap, or on Alt+G.
  It copies on Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on macOS) in every keymap, and now on the keymap's own copy chord too (M-w in Emacs).
- **`-v` prints the version**, as `-V` and `--version` do.
- **The ten Go to Mnemonic bookmark commands have descriptions** in the Command Palette, and their titles follow
  the interface language when it changes.
- **Universal Argument no longer carries a key in its title.** The palette shows the chord your keymap binds to it,
  like every other command.
- **In About, an available update is shown in amber**, so it stands apart from the links beside it.
- **The Debug toolbar and the Markdown format bar separate their groups by spacing**, without a drawn line, as the
  main toolbar does.
- **The Enable plugins setting says on its own row that it needs a restart.** The note used to sit in a separate
  row below it, where a search for the setting did not show it.
- **Settings names its two scopes plainly.** In a project window the top of Settings now reads "Edit settings for
  **All projects** | **This project: name**" instead of "Settings for User | Project: name", with a little space
  between the two buttons and a tooltip on All projects saying it is used in every window unless a project sets its
  own.
- **The editor's right-click menu opens with the editing items.** Cut, Copy and Paste, then Undo and Redo, then
  Select All now come first, in the same place on every file, with Run and Debug, the debugger, LSP, build, AI,
  spelling, markup, comment, plugin, bookmark and note items below them. The breakpoint actions — Toggle, Temporary,
  Recording and Lambda breakpoints, Edit Breakpoint and Enable / Disable — move into one **Breakpoints** submenu,
  which also offers the Breakpoints list and Mute Breakpoints.
- **The Commit window says when a clean tree still has commits to push.** Below "Nothing to commit — working tree
  clean" it now adds "2 commits to push to origin/main" and a Push button, instead of leaving the small `↑2` in the
  header as the only sign. A branch with no upstream keeps the header's `↑ publish` alone.
- **The Map's Project overview opens on every session's first Map open.** The Overview card used to open once per
  workspace, the first time ever; it now opens the first time the Map shows a folder in each session (not again
  when the window is closed and opened again), so a Map opened afresh starts from the project's facts. ⋯ → Project
  overview still opens it at any time.
- **Map cards opened from one column line up.** A second code card opened from a row of the same column stands
  level with the first — flowing left to right or right to left, at the same left edge and below it, in a column of
  cards; flowing down or up, at the same top and right of it, in a row — instead of cascading or going on past it.
- **Pause stops the whole Java program.** It suspended only the thread on screen, and the program's other threads
  kept running. Continue after a Pause resumes every thread.
- **Refactor:** every dialog that is answered with a button is shown through `Dialogs.showAndWait`, or
  `Dialogs.show` where it must not block, which a test answers with no window (`Dialogs.answerWith`,
  `DialogAnswers`), and every question before a destructive action takes its words from a static function
  (`Confirm.Question`, `Confirm.Choice`). No dialog looks or behaves differently (CONF-12, Pauta 6.0.1).
- **Refactor:** Go to Implementation's picker-row text (`implementationLabel`, `implementationDetail`,
  `libraryPackage`) moved from `LspCoordinator` to a new `ImplementationTargets`, which brings `LspCoordinator` back
  under the 10,000-line `SourceFileSizeTest` limit it crossed in #1445.
- **Refactor:** the five largest Java files are split into package-private classes that each own one area, with no
  behaviour change; the old classes keep their API as forwarders.
  - `MainController` (9,979 → 5,416 lines): each coordinator's Host/Ops adapter is a named `*Host` class, plus
    `WindowToolbar`, `EditorTabListeners` and `SettingsWindowWiring`.
  - `EditorBuffer` (9,975 → 5,779): `BufferPreview`, `BufferLayout`, `BufferTyping`, `BufferSnippets`,
    `BufferContextMenu`, `BufferRunGutter`, `BufferInlays`, `BufferRuler`, `BufferHighlighter`, `SelectionBars`,
    `BufferCarets`, `BufferTodos`, `BufferLspAssists`, `BufferNarrowing` and `BufferBanners`.
  - `LspCoordinator` (9,971 → 5,513): `LspWorkspaceEdits`, `WorkspaceEditStaging`, `LspRefactoringUndo`,
    `LspRefactorings`, `LspNavigation`, `LspSuperMethods` and `LspPopups`.
  - `SettingsWindow` (9,857 → 4,941): one class per large settings area (`SettingsLspPage`, `SettingsAiPages`,
    `SettingsSnippetPages`, `SettingsKeymapsPage`, `SettingsSyncPage` and others), each owning its controls, layout
    and load.
  - `LspManager` (8,414 → 4,210): the request families (`LspNavigationRequests`, `LspAssists`, `LspCodeActions`,
    `LspFormatting`, `JdtlsCommands` and others), `ServerInitOptions`, `JdtlsWorkspaces` and the pure
    `WorkspaceEditDrafts`; session lifecycle and locking stay in `LspManager`.
- **Language servers and debugging are no longer marked Beta.** Their Settings pages lose the Beta pill and the
  "Experimental — may be unstable" note.
- **The Map's preview eye closes an open card.** Clicking the eye on a file row whose preview card is open closes
  the card, as Shift+Enter does; its hint says so.
- **A file card's Structure column is narrower.** It fits only the rows it shows (refitting as a row opens or
  closes), between 200 and 360 px, instead of every member of closed rows up to 560 px.
- **Map cards open the way columns do.** With Focus new column on (the default), a new code or note card opens
  where its row's next column would — past the row's column the way the map flows, hanging from the row, past any
  column or card already there — and the map pans to centre it, keeping its row in sight. With the option off, cards
  keep taking free room in view without panning.
- **Language servers are on by default.** Settings → LSP was off, so opening a Java, TypeScript, Go or Rust file
  in a new installation never said code intelligence existed. Each server still waits until it is installed (the
  install banner offers it).
- **Language servers no longer run an untrusted folder's build.** Loading some projects runs their code: a Gradle
  build's scripts, Maven build extensions, Rust build scripts and proc macros, a `Gemfile`, MSBuild projects,
  Leiningen. In a folder you have not trusted, Java now starts without its Maven or Gradle build (syntax checks and
  the JDK's types still work), and the Kotlin, Scala, Rust, Ruby, C# and Clojure servers wait. Their files say so
  and offer **Trust Folder**; trusting restarts them with the build. A folder you trusted before (for example by
  running its `./mvnw`) is unchanged.
- **New defaults for three more settings** (an existing installation keeps the values it has):
  - **Debugging is on.** Settings → Debugging was off, and it is the switch for the Python and JavaScript
    debuggers as well as Java's. Each debugger still waits for its adapter to be found.
  - **Hidden files show in the Project tree and the Map.** `.github/`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore` and `.env`
    are project files; the repository's own `.git` folder (or a worktree's `.git` file) is never listed, with the
    setting on or off.
  - **The Markdown preview asks before loading remote images.** A README from a cloned repository no longer
    fetches its `http`/`https` images the moment it is previewed; a bar offers to load them for that document.
    Settings → Markdown → Remote images → Always restores the old behaviour. A settings file from before 0.22
    that had remote images on keeps loading them.
- **Expert mode hides the menu bar too**, as Zen does. In a window with the menu bar in the title bar only the
  menus leave; the window title and buttons stay. Commands stay on their keys and in the command palette.
- **Every entry in the Project Map's ⋯ menu has an icon**, not only Reveal Active File.
- **`C-x b` (Switch to Buffer) is as tall as `C-x C-f` (Find File).** With a few buffers open it used to come up
  less than half the height.
- **A newer JDK builds Editora.** On JDK 26 and later the build skips the format check (Palantir Java Format runs
  only on JDK 25) and says so, instead of refusing to build.

### Fixed

- **Enter on an empty last line of a Clojure or other Lisp file no longer fails.** With the caret at the very end
  of the file after a line break, Enter threw an error instead of indenting the new line.
- **Debugger review fixes.** A review of the whole debugger found these, now fixed:
  - **Several sessions at once.** A compound of saved Java, Go, Rust or Node configurations launched every member
    into its last session; each now starts its own. A Debug Test attach goes to the session waiting for it, not to
    the one you clicked meanwhile; Stop in one session no longer drops another run's queued JVMs; turning Debug
    support off stops every session; a file opened mid-session lines up breakpoints for every session; hot code
    replace on save reaches every Java session; Thread Dump and Parallel Stacks open frames and take stacks again
    in the session they came from; and breakpoints edited in closed files (Breakpoints list, Map card, import, Mute)
    reach each session as its start would send them, triggered ones held back.
  - **Processes and stuck sessions.** C#'s Debug Test at Caret stops its `dotnet test` run when the attach fails or
    the session, tab or window closes. A debugger that exits while starting (e.g. GDB older than 14) says so, with
    what it printed. Stopping while a TypeScript program's build is checked no longer starts it anyway. A
    `toString()` that timed out no longer blocks Resume and Step for the rest of the session. Stop while connecting
    ends at once, and a Node child ending no longer stalls the session's end. Go's `editora-dlv-*` binaries no
    longer pile up in the temp folder, and closed View as Table windows are freed.
  - **Run to Cursor** reaches its line past logpoints, recording and filtered breakpoints on the way; a stop it shows
    you ends it, as before.
  - **Node workers.** After Thread Dump or Parallel Stacks, variables and evaluation no longer answer from another
    worker; resuming one worker no longer marks the whole session running, and the program's exit code is shown.
  - **launch.json.** Edited files are saved before a configuration starts, and Restart runs its `preLaunchTask` (or
    cargo build) again. A shell task whose command or arguments have spaces runs, on Windows too. A
    `debug-adapters.json` adapter claiming a type Editora handles itself is reported instead of ignored.
  - **Debug window.** Evaluating or adding a watch while an earlier stop is shown no longer overwrites it; Set Value
    typed across a step is refused instead of set in the old stop; the latest of two quick evaluations is the one
    shown; a completion accepted while typing on replaces the word; a value of only line breaks no longer breaks
    Variables; native frames no longer show ":0".
  - **Finding the code.** C# Debug Test at Caret finds the test with helper types above it, in nested test classes
    and with the attribute on the method's line; Go's is not confused by raw strings; a breakpoint below a JavaScript
    regex containing `/*` or a multi-line template literal is no longer refused; Show Value As reads a Java `char`
    such as `'7'` by its code; Attach to Process no longer offers a Node `--inspect=0` program on 9229 and lists
    macOS native and Rust programs with DWARF in a `.dSYM`.
  - **Smaller ones.** Bash debugging has its card in Settings → Debugging; a conditional breakpoint on a Bash
    script's first line no longer pauses at start; a remote JavaScript session no longer shows the last local
    debugger's errors; method breakpoints and field watchpoints are in place before the program starts; reading
    memory more than 2 GB from an address reads the right place; Set Value keeps the typed value when the debugger
    leaves it out.
- **Screen readers can name every control and use the status bar.** Filter fields, lists and trees of the tool
  windows, the palette and pickers, form fields, Settings fields beside a button, and rows built from icons and
  labels (the call stack, variables, Git log, Switcher and others) had no name, so Narrator and VoiceOver said only
  "edit" or "list". Each now reads as its caption or what it shows. Every clickable status-bar segment, the echo
  line included, is a button a screen reader can press, and a new status message is read out. So are the editor's
  problem counter, a Markdown preview's collapsible section, the AI agent's client, model and mode and the file
  paths in its replies, the diff viewer's apply arrows, Parallel Stacks frames, and the lightbulb, breakpoint and
  run marks of the gutter and the Project Map cards. A test runs every
  command, opens every tool window and Settings page, and fails on any control left without a name.
- **Windows open centred on the editor window.** The detached Agent window opened in the middle of the screen,
  and a few error alerts (a template that failed to save, any dialog asked with no window behind it) did too. They
  now open over the editor window in front, centred on it, as Settings, Run Configurations and the debugger windows
  already did. A floating tool window opened for the first time is also kept wholly on the editor's screen.
- **View: Split Tool Window Side shows its picker.** The command found the tool windows that could join a side and
  then showed nothing: its picker had never been given the place it opens in.
- **Six small stalls and wrong answers under load.**
  - The debugger checks in Settings could show an older answer over a newer one when a path was changed
    quickly; an answer is now shown only while it is the newest.
  - The commit graph in the Git Log was painted more than once for one change; it is painted once a frame.
  - The debugger's completion list asked the debugger at every character, and Open File read a folder at every
    folder typed through; both now wait for typing to pause.
  - A fast AI agent reply and the progress of a Git command were handed to the window as they arrived; they
    now arrive in batches a frame apart, as program output does.
  - Import Breakpoints read the chosen file whole, whatever its size; a file over 16 MB is refused.
  - A few background threads had no name or could delay exit; every thread is now named and a daemon.
- **A picker with nothing to list says so.** Jump to Bookmark, Recent Files and the two notes pickers opened
  as a blank card when there was nothing to choose from. Every picker now shows a sentence there, its own
  where it has one ("No bookmarks in this project"), and "No matches" when what you typed matches nothing.
- **Messages with a count say one or several.** "Replaced 1 occurrence(s)", "Updated 3 link(s) in 1 file(s)"
  and 20 more messages now word the count in each of the six languages: "Replaced 1 occurrence", "3 liens
  mis à jour dans 1 fichier". The translations had each invented a notation for it ("Datei(en)",
  "immagine/i", "ligação(ões)").
- **Line numbers in messages are no longer grouped like quantities.** Messages that name a line, a column,
  a port or a process id showed "line 1,234" past line 999 (or "1.234" in German).
- **Two labels were English in every language**: the line number beside a bookmark in the Bookmarks panel,
  and the find bar's in-selection toggle.
- **The debugger's toolbar shows the new keys after a keymap switch.** Continue, Step Over and the other
  buttons of the Debug window kept the old keymap's keys in their tooltips until the next debug session
  changed state.
- **A closed project window is released from memory.** Closing a project window left the whole window in memory,
  with its files, panels and tools, until Editora quit, so memory grew with every project opened and closed. The No
  Project window stayed the same way once its Project Map had been opened, and so did the last window to run Import
  Configuration. All three are released now when the window closes.
- **Deleting a file on Windows moves it to the Recycle Bin.** Delete in the Project tree, Move Original to
  Trash after encrypting, and the clean-up of unused pasted images deleted for good on Windows, where
  Editora reached no trash at all. They now use the Recycle Bin, as Explorer does, for files on a local
  drive. A file on a network share, a WSL distribution or a removable drive has no Recycle Bin, and the
  question before deleting it still says the delete cannot be undone. Linux and macOS are unchanged.
- **Save as Administrator is grayed on Windows, and says why.** It was offered there in the File menu, the
  command palette and Settings, and did nothing: Windows has no prompt Editora can ask for administrator
  rights for one save. The command, its toggle and the Settings row are still listed, disabled, with that
  reason. Linux and macOS are unchanged.
- **Logpoints work in C#.** netcoredbg doesn't support logpoints, so a C# logpoint stopped the program like a plain
  breakpoint and logged nothing. When a debugger can't log logpoints itself, Editora now logs the message in the Debug
  console, with each `{expression}` evaluated where the program stopped, and lets it go on. The editor is not taken to
  the line, and the stop is not kept in Debug History. The program pauses briefly at each hit, as it does for a
  logpoint with `$FUNCTION` or another token. A condition on the logpoint still decides when it logs.
- **Compare With… on a background tab compares that tab's file.** Right-clicking a tab that was not the active one
  and choosing Compare With… compared the active file with the one you picked. Every other row of the tab menu
  already acted on the tab you clicked.
- **One-key shortcuts for Go to Line, Related File, the matching bracket and Back / Forward work in a Project Map
  card.** A card runs these on its own text and file, but only a multi-key chord reached it: Ctrl+G (Go to Line in the
  CUA, VS Code, Sublime and IntelliJ keymaps), Ctrl+Shift+T (Related File in IntelliJ) and the like did nothing while
  a card had the keyboard, and Emacs's `C-M-a` / `C-M-e` did not move to a definition's start or end. Back and
  Forward typed on the Map itself now walk its history from a one-key chord too. The card menu's **Go to Line…** and
  **Related Test / Subject** rows show their shortcut.
- **An unexpected error now shows a message in the status bar.** An uncaught exception was written to the
  Application Log and nothing else, so the action you took simply did nothing. The status bar now says an
  unexpected error occurred and where the details are, at most once every ten seconds.
- **Shift+Enter in the editor's find field steps to the previous match.** Enter stepped forward, and the previous
  match had no key in the field.
- **The numbers in the heaviest cells of the Project Map's dependency matrix are readable in every theme.** Their
  color named a token no theme defines.
- **A French message about Maven versions showed "nont" for "n'ont".**
- **Local History limits and the auto-save delay in a hand-edited `settings.json` are kept within their ranges.** A
  limit of 0 snapshots for a file, or an auto-save delay of 0, was taken as written.
- **A desktop notification that cannot be shown is recorded in the Application Log**, with the program that failed
  and why. The failure was dropped without a trace.
- **A match-case button of a Project Map card's find bar can be reached with Tab.**
- **Waiting for a debugged Java program's exit code, and seven other disk reads, no longer run on the JVM's
  shared worker pool**, where a slow disk could hold up unrelated background work.
- **A breakpoint could be missed at the very start of a JavaScript program.** Debugging told js-debug to run the
  program before js-debug had placed the breakpoints, so one near the start (a breakpoint inside an arrow function
  most often) was sometimes passed by. Editora now waits for the breakpoints to be placed first, as VS Code does.
- **A Project Map card opened from a hierarchy tree no longer closes on its own.** When its file's folder was not
  open on the map, the next folder change could close it. It now stays while the card the tree was asked from is
  open, as other result cards do.
- **The build trust prompt names the project's build command, not yours.** In a folder not yet trusted, the
  build trust prompt listed the command set in your own Settings as if the project's `.editora/settings.json` ran
  it, and never listed a command the project file does set — the one trusting the folder would apply. It now lists
  the project file's command whenever there is one, and the file's right name.
- **`.http` results stay on their requests after a line is added above them.** A request's last result after its
  line could vanish, with the ■ drawn on the old lines for a moment, when a line was added above the requests while
  the editor was still finding them in the text from before the edit; that out-of-date answer is now dropped and
  the edit's own scan places them.
- **Settings help links open the right section.** The **?** on Code Completion and Spell Check opened the
  Editing page and Mermaid's the Diagrams page, none of which covers them; they now open Autocomplete and Spell
  checking on the Languages page and Mermaid diagrams on the Markdown page. The Sync page's subtitle and *Sync Now*
  name shortcuts among what is synced.
- **The Map's cards keep their places.** Where the open preview cards stand (with the open folders, selection, zoom
  and pan) is now saved to disk moments after it changes, not only when the session ends cleanly, so a card moved
  before a crash or a kill comes back where it was; and a card brought back with its Structure column out is no
  longer nudged for the column, so it stands where it was left.
- **The window buttons show with a dark theme.** On Linux, minimise, maximise and close were drawn dark grey on
  the dark title bar, all but invisible, whenever the theme was dark and the desktop's was not: JavaFX styles the
  window frame and its buttons from the desktop's light or dark setting. Every window, dialogs included, now takes
  it from Editora's theme, as it opens and when the theme changes.
- **The Emacs keymap no longer lists `M-g s` twice.** The key was bound to both Search Notes and Go to Symbol in
  Workspace; only Go to Symbol ever ran, while the command catalogs showed `M-g s` for Search Notes too. Search Notes
  is a palette command, and a test now rejects any keymap file that lists a chord twice.
- **A trail stop's note no longer covers its card.** Since cards open centred, a wide card could leave too little
  room for the note on either side, and the note was laid over the stop's lines (on macOS at the default size).
  The map now pans just far enough for the note to stand beside the card.
- **Map caller and reference cards no longer pile up.** With Focus new column on, Show Callers or References as
  Cards opened every result card on one spot, at full width, instead of beside the card asked from. Each now opens
  beside that card at the narrower result width, in a place of its own, stacking above or below the ones there.
- **An open Problems window follows Next / Previous Problem.** The editor's problem-counter arrows (and F2 /
  Shift+F2) select the problem they step to in the Problems tool window, opening its folded header and scrolling
  it into view, while the focus stays in the editor — even when the last click was in the Problems window.
- **Map Print and Export PDF include the open cards.** Preview, note and Overview cards, what is stuck on them
  (sticky notes, Structure columns, link chips) and their connectors are drawn on the pages where they stand on the
  map, as on screen; the pages grow to take in a card standing beyond the columns. Export ▸ SVG still leaves the
  cards out.
- **Alt-Backspace (`M-DEL`) deletes the word before the caret in text fields** such as Find File, every picker and
  prompt; in a path it takes one folder at a time. It did nothing there.
- **The debugger's value popup shows an arrow, and a hand over its rows**, not the editor's I-beam.
- **The Debug tool window's columns have padding**, and turning on the Threads view no longer moves the toggle.
- **A Project Map card no longer misses a change made while it was reading the file.** It kept the old text, and
  its problem markers, until the next poll.
